{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-nm-x","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"472ef9fb9be858f81d14d908d0a9bf30b68c9c038d161804eea4b0f48c0b3a05","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-nm-class-std:lineage:40","source_registry_sha256":"22599efcb4852b796972acef6eb09f4cfe8d16ca15887f7ea7660c7748b4df92","source_liveness_sha256":"6766993f61347d495f390e08c7d8b1c44de597b6249cdb10686ea7f9f38e1ea3"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C2"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C2","chunk_id":"C2.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Pavement markings and lane controls","heading":"C2 — Pavement markings and lane controls","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"## C2 — Pavement markings and lane controls

FACT_ID: sec04-R01 | anchor: A02
A reversible lane carries traffic in opposite directions at different times. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec04-R02 | anchor: A02
Reversible lanes are commonly marked by paired broken yellow lines. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec04-R03 | anchor: A02
Before entering a reversible lane, check the current lane-use signs or signals. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec04-R04 | anchor: A02
A green overhead arrow permits use of the lane directly below it. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec04-R05 | anchor: A02
A red overhead X prohibits driving in the lane below it. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec04-R06 | anchor: A02
A flashing yellow overhead X limits the lane to turning. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec04-R07 | anchor: A02
A steady yellow overhead X warns of a lane-use change and calls for leaving the lane as soon as safe. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec04-R08 | anchor: A02
A reserved lane is identified by signs describing the permitted use and often by a white diamond. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec04-R09 | anchor: A02
A lane labeled Transit or Bus is reserved for buses. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec04-R10 | anchor: A02
A lane labeled Bicycle is reserved for bicycle travel. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec04-R11 | anchor: A02
HOV means high-occupancy vehicles and identifies a lane for vehicles carrying more than one person. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec04-R12 | anchor: A02
The sign for an HOV lane specifies the required occupancy and the days and hours of the restriction. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec04-R13 | anchor: A02
An HOV three sign requires at least three occupants in the vehicle. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec04-R14 | anchor: A02
A shared center lane is reserved for left turns and permitted U-turns, and vehicles from either direction may use it for those turns. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec04-R15 | anchor: A02
Alternating left-turn arrows show the movements permitted from a shared middle lane. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec04-R16 | anchor: A02
A shared middle lane is bounded on each side by a solid yellow line paired with a broken yellow line. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec04-R17 | anchor: A02
Some shared middle lanes become reversible during peak traffic periods, so entry requires checking that the lane is available and safe. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec04-R18 | anchor: A02
When signs and markings do not assign lane use, general driving, passing and turning rules determine the lane to use. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0012]
